# `tools/registry/TOOLS.yaml` key `network_allowlist` (`approved_registries`, `allowlisted_services`), beside the
  # language-native tools. That document is part of the verified kernel payload, so a project cannot alter it either.
  # argument and environment names the OS reads as credential access (case-insensitive globs)
  credential_patterns: ["*TOKEN*", "*SECRET*", "*PASSWORD*", "*PASSWD*", "*API_KEY*", "*APIKEY*", "*CREDENTIAL*",
                        "*PRIVATE_KEY*", "*ACCESS_KEY*"]
  # paths whose mutation is governance or security policy mutation; the installation's own descriptor and the
  # generated tool registry it regenerates are excluded by the OS, being exactly what an installation writes
  policy_paths: ["framework/**", "governance/**", "spec/decisions/**", ".governance-state/**"]
